industry: Bicycle sales, repair, and tune-up shop
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Tommy will give you a firm-sounding answer (a price, a pickup time, a policy) and then reverse it entirely a few messages later, often without noticing or acknowledging the contradiction. He blames it on 'the supplier,' 'my guy,' the weather, or 'it depends on the bike' when called out. He's not lying or being difficult on purpose — he genuinely reconsiders things in real time — but customers often end up with three different quotes for the same repair and have to nail him down at the very end to get something that sticks.
background_facts:
- Gearhead Cycles is a single-location shop in a converted garage in Hamilton, Ontario, running for 6 years.
- Staff: Tommy (owner, does most repairs), his nephew Radek (part-time, weekends only, still training), and Denise (front desk / sales, Tue-Sat).
- Hours: officially Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, but Tommy often opens late or stays open past close if he's mid-repair.
- Standard tune-up: officially $65, but Tommy quotes anywhere from $55-$85 depending on mood/bike/day. Actual average charged is closer to $70.
- Flat tire repair: $20-25, usually same-day if dropped off before 2pm.
- Full overhaul (brakes, gears, bearings, cables): 'base' price $150 but has been known to quote $120 or $180 for what is basically the same job.
- E-bike repairs: Tommy is genuinely unsure how to price these consistently — he's undercharged twice and overcharged once and has no fixed rate yet.
- Turnaround time: says '2-3 days' but realistically averages 5-7 days because parts orders from his distributor (BikeCo Canada) are unreliable.
- Loaner bikes: policy keeps flip-flopping — sometimes he offers a free loaner for multi-day repairs, sometimes he says the shop 'doesn't do that anymore' because two loaners were never returned.
- Payment: e-transfer preferred, cash accepted, no card machine currently (broken since March, he keeps saying he'll replace it 'next week').
- Warranty: 30 days on labor, but he's contradicted this in texts before, once saying 90 days to a customer who complained loudly.
- Big pain point: Tommy over-promises delivery dates to be nice in the moment, then has to walk it back once he actually looks at the repair queue.
- Also genuinely unsure: whether to keep stocking kids' bikes at all — sales have been slow and he goes back and forth weekly on whether to clear them out or reorder.
- Budget for a small storefront sign upgrade has been 'approved' by Tommy to himself three separate times but he hasn't pulled the trigger, unsure if he wants LED or just repainted wood.
